doc.title: Dave Liebman — Smithsonian Jazz Oral History

title: Jazz as a model of improvisation and democratic values
summary: Kirchner cites Toffler on improvisers; Liebman says jazz embodies positive democratic values that no autocratic culture would produce.

story.theme_name: Late-career reflections: awards, legacy and life lessons
story.community_name: Life philosophy: faith, karma and how to live

blocks.x: I tell my students, you’re learning to be a jazz musician, and that involves learning to be an improviser. One of the things you have to learn is how to improvise as a career. That’s what we all do. Did you ever read a book called The Third Wave, by Alvin Toffler?
He was – his heroes were jazz musicians, because jazz musicians could think on their feet and were much more flexible and could change directions rapidly.

Yeah, we’re becoming the model, and we’re becoming a corporate model now. Guys going out and giving these clinics, right?, how to hit a conga drum, because, feel your inner Jones, make up the thing. Oh, be a little looser in your stuff. Yeah, there are a lot of great qualities to this music that are intrinsic to learning the music. But it’s more than that. It’s the lifestyle. I don’t mean the negative part. That’s understood. We got that. Bird, the movie, took care of that. It’s the positive, life-affirming values that this music represents, from Louis Armstrong, from Jelly [Roll Morton], I don’t care, the little I know about them, to today, kids, those two guys who just walked out of here. This is positive, period. There is not one negative bone of anything in this music. I never heard of music being negative, resentful, hateful, jealous, contemptible. Music is what we bring to it, and this music, above all, is American. It’s democracy. You would not have found this in China, my friend. You’re not going to find this in an autocratic culture. This is not the top down. This is about us all, level playing field. One guy stands out. Then he comes back. Basketball.
That’s right. There was a reason why the Nazis hated jazz.
